interviewQuestions.question: YOLO vs Faster R-CNN — which do you pick for a real-time app?
interviewQuestions.answerMarkdown:
I'd start by naming the actual trade-off: Faster R-CNN is a two-stage detector — it proposes candidate regions first, then classifies and refines each one — which generally gives higher accuracy, especially on small or overlapping objects, but at real cost in speed, typically running well under 15 fps. YOLO is one-stage — a single network pass predicts all boxes and classes at once — which is what makes it capable of real-time throughput, often 30+ fps or higher depending on the variant and hardware. For a real-time app — say, a live camera feature or an autonomous-driving perception module — I'd pick YOLO, because meeting the latency budget is a hard constraint the product cannot function without, whereas the accuracy gap versus Faster R-CNN has narrowed substantially in recent YOLO versions and is often an acceptable trade for staying real-time. I'd only reconsider this if the specific objects being detected are very small relative to the frame (where two-stage detectors historically hold a bigger edge) or if the app can tolerate offline/batch processing instead of live inference.

**Testing:** whether you can articulate the actual speed/accuracy trade-off with correct reasoning, rather than just naming YOLO as the default answer without justification.
interviewQuestions.subTitle: One-stage vs two-stage for a latency-critical product
